html:
The Kamia were the eastern, desert branch of the Kumeyaay people, living in the Imperial Valley of southern California and the nearby part of Baja California. They spoke a Yuman language.

Unlike the coastal Kumeyaay, the Kamia farmed. When the Colorado River flooded and spilled into the New River and Alamo River channels, they planted maize, beans and melons in the wet silt, as their neighbours the Quechan did on the river itself. They also gathered mesquite beans and seeds. Their descendants are counted among the Kumeyaay bands today.
